subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination (Acme)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & next steps

Alex \u0014 thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up a customer-led load test with your SREs.

Recap / SLO targets you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for inference (text generation) under normal traffic
- Throughput target: 200 req/s sustained for peak scenario
- Concurrency: up to 50 concurrent requests from your app instances
- Streaming: require token-by-token streaming / chunked responses for UX (WebSocket or HTTP chunked stream)
- Error budget tolerance: <1% 5xx during the test window

Proposed next steps:
1) Customer-led load test: we provide a k6 script (or Locust) and a test account; you run from your infra to validate routing and latency from your region.
2) Test window: please propose 2-hour windows when you can run the load. We prefer non-business hours for isolation but will coordinate.
3) IP allowlist: let us know the IP ranges to allowlist or we can provide our test runner IPs.
4) Pre-test checklist: we will share a short checklist (auth, headers, streaming flags).

I attached a base k6 script (acme_k6_base_test.js) with placeholders for API key and endpoint. Will loop in Rishi (SE) and Aditya (SRE) as we prep infra-side.

Thanks \u0014 looking forward to getting this scheduled.

\u0014
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Logan \u0014 good recap. Confirming the targets from our side: p95 <= 150ms, 200 req/s sustained, 50 concurrent. Streaming is important for the UI flow; we prefer to validate both HTTP chunked and WebSocket variants.

Proposed test window options:
- Tue 2027-03-08 14:00-16:00 PST (preferred)
- Wed 2027-03-09 22:00-00:00 PST (backup)

IP allowlist request: please provide the source IPs your test runners will use OR we can provide our outbound ranges if you prefer us to run from our infra. For now, here are the IP ranges we can allowlist on our side: 34.120.32.0/22, 35.196.64.0/20. If Redwood is running public runners, please give the CIDRs.

Test account: we can stand up a scoped test account. Credentials (we'll send via secure channel) should have read-only access to the test workspace and a rate-limited API key.

Pre-test items we care about:
- Auth headers & token expiry behavior
- Streaming mode flags and fallback behavior when streaming isn't available
- Whether token batching changes p95 behavior

Looping in our SRE (sre@acme.com) to align on network allowlists and run ownership.

Alex \u0014 thanks for the options. We can run the test either from our public runners or provide the k6 script for you to run from your infra. To make the run reproducible and to validate routing/latency from your network, I recommend your SRE run it from inside Acme.

Attached: acme_k6_base_test.js (contains scenarios for steady 200 req/s and a surge profile), plus acme_test_account_readme.txt with placeholder credentials and instructions.

Quick notes for whoever runs it:
- Endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (use the test API key in the readme)
- Header: Authorization: Bearer TEST-ACME-XXXX
- Streaming: set header X-Redwood-Stream: chunked to exercise streaming path
- Concurrency in k6: the script includes options forvus to target 50 VUs; update vus and duration variables as needed
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95 latency, overall RPS, 5xx count, connection failures, time-to-first-byte for streaming frames

If you want, our SE (Rishi) can run a short smoke test first from our runner and then hand the script to your SRE for the full window.

Are you able to confirm Tue 2027-03-08 14:00-16:00 PST? If so, please confirm allowlist entries you plan to add and we'll coordinate start-of-test messages.

Thanks \u0014 I can also jump on a 15m pre-test call Monday if that helps.

\u0014
Logan Wright
